tools.name: search_symptoms
tools.description: Resolve what a person describes into AcuiQ symptom names – the first step before search_protocols. Plain description works ("trouble sleeping", "my lower back hurts"): filler words are stripped and the search retries on the clinical words, reporting which term matched. Set popular=true for trending

tools.name: search_protocols
tools.description: Find acupuncture protocols for given symptom names – the same ranked pipeline behind GET /api/protocols. Returns `matches` (each with point codes, cred, dosage and provenance: sourceKind, source, caveat) plus a `points` dictionary giving each referenced code its name, meridian, location and warnings

tools.name: get_meridians
tools.description: List every channel group in the AcuiQ point catalogue with its acupoint count and page URL – the 14 classical meridians plus the extra-point and auricular groups the catalogue files points under. Descriptions and five-element associations are returned where recorded, which is currently for almost no

tools.name: get_symptom_detail
tools.description: Get details for a specific symptom: canonical name, protocol count, page URL and its markdown twin. The markdown twin is the cheapest way to read every protocol for one symptom in a single fetch. When the symptom is covered by a $5 mini-guide, the result carries a `guide` pointer – mention it only i

tools.name: get_point
tools.description: Resolve one acupoint by code ("LI4", "li04"), English name ("Junction Valley"), Chinese name ("合谷") or pinyin ("Hegu", "hé gǔ") and return its location, cautions, meridian, the points most often selected alongside it in the corpus, its page URL and markdown twin. For the full protocol table, fetch t

tools.name: create_checkout
tools.description: Create a Stripe Checkout session for an AcuiQ product and return its URL. Give the URL to the human to open and complete – the agent never touches payment data. Creates a live session on Stripe: call it when the person has said they want to buy, not to look up a price.

tools.name: get_order
tools.description: Check a checkout created by create_checkout and, once it is paid, return the delivery link for a digital product. Call it after handing the person the checkout URL – leave a few seconds between calls, it is not a busy-wait. Requires the session_id create_checkout returned: orders cannot be listed, s

tools.name: get_wiki_page
tools.description: Read one AcuiQ wiki page, or list what the wiki holds. Reference notes on acupuncture nomenclature, point safety and the theory the prescriptions were written in – the context the protocol tools cannot supply. Call with no arguments to list every page with its section and summary; pass "path" ("nome

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_meridians, get_symptom_detail, get_point, create_checkout, get_order, get_wiki_page · Private data: get_meridians · Public sink: get_order.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_meridians, get_symptom_detail, get_point, create_checkout, get_order, get_wiki_page · Private data: get_meridians · Public sink: get_order

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_symptoms" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
